title: Botez Odds Match | Grandmaster Naroditsky Gambit?!?

moves.spoken: Black answers with c5, the Sicilian.
Black fianchettoes with g6, and White replies c3 — the Alapin idea, preparing to seize the centre with d4.
teaches: c3 prepares d4 against the fianchetto Sicilian

moves.spoken: The bishop comes to g7, glaring down the long diagonal.
White builds the full centre with d4, and after the trades holds a broad pawn duo.
Black hits back with d5, but White snaps it off — and pockets a clean pawn in the process.
teaches: A premature ...d5 can simply drop a pawn to the exd5 break

moves.spoken: Black develops the knight to f6 to chase the extra pawn, and White props it up with the bishop to c4 — the setup White knows and trusts.
Black's bishop shuffles to d7, a passive post, and the engine already reads White better than a pawn up: extra material and the freer game.
The knight develops to c3, reinforcing the extra d5-pawn, and Black castles.
White nudges the bishop back to b3 — out of harm's way, still guarding d5 — and castles. Everything is defended and the pawn stands.
teaches: Retreat the bishop to keep it defending the key pawn

moves.spoken: White begins rerouting the knight from c3 toward the kingside, while Black rolls the queenside pawns forward.
teaches: Reroute a knight toward the action rather than leave it passive

moves.spoken: The knight reaches f4 — an aggressive square eyeing e6, g6, and the d5 support — as Black keeps pushing on the flank.
White centralizes the rook to e1, stacking force behind the passed pawn.
And the knight lands on e5 — a monster outpost the pawns can't touch. The evaluation leaps: White is now winning by a clear margin, the whole board bending toward that central knight.
teaches: A knight on e5 backed by a passed pawn is a decisive trump
plans: Push the passed d-pawn behind it

moves.spoken: The passed pawn drives to d6, splitting Black's camp in two and freezing his pieces — the engine now sees it as good as won.
teaches: A passed pawn on the sixth cramps and divides the defense

moves.spoken: The pawn to g4 attacks the bishop on f5 and simply wins it — with two knights swarming, the tactics all fall White's way.
The knights crash through, White collects material, and the position is overwhelming.
